notes.summary: These questions replace signs with other symbols, ask which two signs to interchange, or hide a number in a pattern. Always apply BODMAS after substituting.

concepts.title: BODMAS
concepts.body: Order: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. Do ÷ and × (left to right) before + and −.

concepts.title: Symbol substitution
concepts.body: Rewrite the whole expression with the real signs first, then solve with BODMAS.

concepts.title: Missing number
concepts.body: Find a rule that works for every complete row or pair (sum of squares, product, a × b + c), then apply it to the incomplete one.

varieties.name: Symbol substitution
varieties.how: Replace each symbol with its meaning, then use BODMAS.

varieties.name: Interchange of signs
varieties.how: Swap the two signs in the given expression for each option and solve; the correct one equals the right side.

varieties.name: Missing number
varieties.how: Test sum, product, squares on the complete rows.

tips: Rewrite the expression on paper before solving; most mistakes come from mixing old and new signs.
In interchange questions, use the options: only 4 swaps to test.
traps: Do not solve left to right ignoring BODMAS.
A rule must work for every given row, not just one.

questions.q:
If '+' means '×', '−' means '+', '×' means '÷' and '÷' means '−', then find the value of:
8 + 2 − 6 × 3 ÷ 1

Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
16 + 4 × 3 − 6 ÷ 2 = 11
questions.solution:
Swap − and ×: 16 + 4 − 3 × 6 ÷ 2.
3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 9.
16 + 4 − 9 = 11 ✓.
(Other swaps give 8, 7 and about 5.33.)

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following table.
4541
6240
37?

If A $ B means A + B, A # B means A − B and A @ B means A × B, then what is the value of:
12 @ 3 # 18 $ 4

Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
18 ÷ 3 − 4 × 2 + 5 = 9
